tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand the application as an AI-enabled discussion service. It introduces the Spring Boot backend, Ionic React frontend, Python AI worker, PostgreSQL and pgvector storage, and the AWS deployment path used throughout the tour.

tour.title: Spring Startup Configuration
tour.description: BackendApplication starts the Spring Boot application context. The application properties connect database, authentication, mail, economy data, AI worker, and proxy settings, showing how the components from the overview are assembled at runtime.

tour.title: Board API Boundary
tour.description: BoardPostController accepts requests for posts, comments, tags, likes, reports, and notifications. BoardPostDtos keeps the external JSON contract separate from domain objects, forming a stable boundary between clients and the server model.

tour.title: Service Data Flow
tour.description: Requests from the API boundary reach BoardPostService, where authorization, transactions, response mapping, and RAG indexing rules are coordinated. BoardPostRepository encapsulates persistence queries while the BoardPost aggregate owns post state and domain changes, completing the Controller to Service to Repository to Entity flow.
tour.languageLesson: Spring constructor injection lets the container assemble controllers, services, and repositories while making implementations easy to replace in tests. Transactional service boundaries group multiple persistence operations into one atomic unit.

tour.title: Authentication Security Chain
tour.description: SecurityConfig assembles authorization rules and filter ordering before requests reach controllers. The JWT cookie and CSRF filters protect request boundaries, while AuthService and JwtService manage login use cases and token lifecycles.

tour.title: Spring AI Bridge
tour.description: AgentController receives AI execution requests and AgentService coordinates runs, messages, and evidence state. HttpAgentWorkerClient isolates the Python worker protocol, while AgentRunRepository and AgentDtos separate persistence from the public API representation.

tour.title: Async AI Worker
tour.description: The FastAPI entry point manages worker lifespan, bearer authentication, briefing, and chat endpoints before delegating orchestration to the service module. Guardrails reject unsupported answers, while MCP tools and the discussion retriever supply economy, news, and Spring RAG evidence.
tour.languageLesson: Python async and await allow external API calls, MCP tools, and data searches to overlap without occupying a thread during network waits. FastAPI lifespan and dependency injection separate shared client cleanup and authentication from endpoint logic.

tour.title: React Client Flow
tour.description: The browser entry point mounts the application and App composes routing, internationalization, themes, and feature pages. The shared backend client handles sessions and XSRF, while the agent API and workbench call Spring endpoints and render evidence links and execution traces.
tour.languageLesson: React components and hooks separate presentation state from side effects. Providers placed in the application shell share theme and language state without repeatedly passing props through every feature page.

tour.title: Flyway Schema Evolution
tour.description: The first migration creates board and RAG foundations, followed by users and preferences, then agent runs, messages, and MCP evidence. The agent_runs table connects the AgentService and repository state from earlier steps to concrete columns and constraints.
tour.languageLesson: Flyway migrations should be applied cumulatively in version order, and deployed files should be extended with new migrations instead of edited in place. Foreign keys and indexes improve integrity and read performance but add write cost, so they should follow real query paths.

tour.title: Layered Regression Tests
tour.description: ApiIntegrationTests covers broad server paths, LoginSecurityTests protects authentication boundaries, and HttpAgentWorkerClientTests verifies the Spring to Python protocol. The Python pytest suite and fixtures independently check guardrails, localized fallbacks, MCP policy, RAG conversion, and schemas to prevent regressions across runtimes.

tour.title: Container Runtime Boundaries
tour.description: The backend Dockerfile packages the Maven-based Spring application into an executable container image. The worker Dockerfile installs the Python application on a slim runtime and starts Uvicorn on port 8090, keeping Java and Python as independent deployment units.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds separate compilation tools from the minimal runtime image, reducing size and attack surface. Placing stable dependency installation before frequently changing source copies improves layer cache reuse.

tour.title: CI Deployment Automation
tour.description: The CI workflow runs backend tests and frontend validation and builds in parallel to enforce the quality gates from the testing step. The AWS role workflow checks GitHub OIDC integration, while the automation workflow performs ECS deployment and operational verification, completing the path from source change to production.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions YAML uses on for triggers, jobs for parallel units, and steps for sequential commands. OIDC replaces long-lived AWS access keys with short-lived credentials issued for each workflow run.
